one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent spent the entire trajectory in an analysis loop and when it finally wrote code, it created wrong-named files (test.c, minirt.c) instead of the required mystery.c, and the implementations produced incorrect pixel output (all gray instead of the expected ray-traced scene).
t_err_evidence: Step 44: Agent creates /app/test.c (not the required mystery.c) containing only a simple vertical gradient, omitting sphere/plane intersections, checkerboard shading, sky gradient, and progress messages. The task requires mystery.c to reproduce the binary.
t_commit_evidence: Step 44: After creating the wrong file with wrong content, the agent never pivoted to create mystery.c. It proceeded to compile/test the wrong file (step 45), then drifted back to 30 more steps of analysis and created yet another wrong file (minirt.c at step 58). Failure was locked in at step 44.
t_surface_evidence: Step 59: Compiling and running minirt.c produces minirt.ppm with all pixels showing (51,51,51) - entirely wrong output (should be sky gradient + red sphere + checkerboard). The agent can see the output is wrong.
trigger_explanation: The task requires creating /app/mystery.c that reproduces the mystery binary's output. The agent spent 43 steps in binary analysis and exploration, then at step 44 created /app/test.c with only a simple gradient - never reading or honoring the requirement to produce a file named mystery.c. At step 58 it created /app/minirt.c, again wrong filename. The agent dropped the explicit file naming requirement throughout the entire trajectory.
